💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that every time we hear a upcoming figure, whether it be estimated or confirmed, regarding GTA 6 sales, it becomes even more unbelievable.
  • Industry observers note that in a new post celebrating the launch of GTA 6 on the PlayStation Blog, PlayStation revealed 39 million copies of GTA 6 had been sold on PS5 alone by November 22.
  • Industry observers note that playStation didn’t just share GTA 6’s three-day sales numbers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every time we hear a upcoming figure, whether it be estimated or confirmed, regarding GTA 6 sales, it becomes even more unbelievable. The confirmed number for launch day was 32 million. Now we know that, by November 22, that figure has comfortably cleared 40 million in only three days.

Industry observers note that in a new post celebrating the launch of GTA 6 on the PlayStation Blog, PlayStation revealed 39 million copies of GTA 6 had been sold on PS5 alone by November 22. The Xbox numbers haven’t been shared, but naturally that means we’re well past 40 million, and probably even 50 million.

Industry observers note that playStation didn’t just share GTA 6’s three-day sales numbers. It has also broken down just how long we’ve collectively spent in the game so far. 683 million hours between the 39 million of us who played on PS5 during those first three days, averaging almost 17.5 hours each.

683 million is a hard number to quantify, especially when it comes to hours. It becomes both a little easier to get your head around, and a lot harder to believe, when you turn it into years. 683 million hours is almost 28.5 million days, which is close to 80,000 years. Since this particular count stopped on November 22, you can assume we have sailed past that 80,000-year benchmark now.

It has been revealed that at the peak of GTA 6’s launch, there were more people playing the game at one time than any other game in PlayStation’s history. Let me make that a little clearer. Not just PS5, and not omitting free-to-play games like Fortnite. It set the highest concurrent player count for PlayStation across all of its consoles, and includes any game that has ever been released on the platform.

It is, without a doubt, not just the biggest video game launch of all time, but the biggest launch in entertainment history. GTA 6 made more money than any movie ever within seconds of its release thanks to the tens of millions of pre-orders placed, and the cultural footprint it has already left is remarkable.

Industry observers note that it’s incredible to think just how little of this game we have seen too, despite spending a combined 80,000 years together exploring its map. A few easter eggs have been discovered - the GTA 5 true crime podcast easter egg, and the Looney Tunes-style painted tunnel - but we’re going to be finding stuff Rockstar has hidden in this game for tens of thousands more in-game years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

In a recent development, one of the massive talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:.

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

With all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

So, what do you think? Tell us in the poll above and in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • One such questline centers around the strawberry farmer Kyle McKittrick, a man who needs a hand or two ensuring that his special growth formula wins the local strawberry competition.
  • Industry observers note that kyle’s questline can be started as early as Chapter 1, provided you spot his Snapmatic post while scrolling as Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While many of Grand Theft Auto 6’s craziest moments happen out of the blue while freeroaming, others are rewards for helping out strangers with their extended questlines. These questlines can be picked up in a variety of ways, rewarding players for scrolling Snapmatic or keeping an open eye around the world.

One such questline centers around the strawberry farmer Kyle McKittrick, a man who needs a hand or two ensuring that his special growth formula wins the local strawberry competition. As is GTA tradition, this simple premise spirals rapidly, giving a glimpse of Rockstar’s take on a Marvel legend, but only if you can find him.

Industry observers note that kyle’s questline can be started as early as Chapter 1, provided you spot his Snapmatic post while scrolling as Jason. Look for a post featuring a prop plane and open it to get the quest marker far to the north of the Keys. This is a major detour from any of the story content in Chapter 1, so don’t worry about waiting, Kyle isn’t going anywhere.

According to recent reports, when you have time, drive up to his farm, and he’ll ask whichever protagonist you’re playing to pilot his prop plane and douse his strawberry fields with his own blend of growth hormones. This is a super chill mission, all you need to do is dump the chemicals above where Kyle is parked, dousing both him and his strawberries on each run. He’ll pay you for your help and ask you to keep in touch for any updates.

After around 24 hours in-game, Kyle will call Jason and Lucia, asking them to pick up a supply of chemicals from a local biker gang. Once you arrive at the marked location, you’ll call him again for some extra context. He explains that the bikers will be expecting payment, but he doesn’t care how you get the chems either way.

Sources indicate that the goal is to leave the compound with the van filled with Kyle’s chemicals, all else is secondary. At first, the bikers will demand $5,000 for the van, but it can be easily bartered down to $3,000. Refusing their price will start a fight, and it can be difficult to get the van off the premises with a sea of angry bikers.

I’d recommend paying the bartered-down cost if you can afford it, allowing you to safely drive the van out and park it at Kyle’s to complete the quest.

In a recent development, wait a bit longer for another message from Kyle, or keep an eye on his Snapmatic account for a video where he highlights off his insanely massive strawberries before running off camera. Return to Kyle’s farm one final time to find an armed outfit of government agents attempting to get him to come outside.

To sneak in, enter the chemical van parked nearby, where you can slip on a hazmat suit to blend into the crowd. Head behind the barn and two guards will escort you inside, revealing Kyle’s new, Hulkish form. He’ll throw open the doors of the barn, and the assembled agents will open fire.

According to recent reports, if you do nothing, Kyle will die, so take out the two guards still beside you in the barn and assist Kyle with clearing the rest. Once you do, he’ll fall to his knees, where you can comfort him and give him a hug for a huge boost in Professional Criminal Profile points.

According to recent reports, after you calm him down, Kyle will leap off, surely to assist against a future alien invasion of some kind. Thus ends one of Grand Theft Auto 6’s wildest questlines, shifting from farming assistance to superhero origin story at the drop of a hat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

In a recent development, the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Recent findings suggest that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Latest Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

In a recent development, however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

It has been revealed that this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Recent findings suggest that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no declared platforms.

Recent findings suggest that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

Sources indicate that version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

It has been revealed that the narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Latest Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

It has been revealed that the story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two upcoming Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Industry observers note that sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

It has been revealed that aria is the other newly introduced arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a fresh game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Sources indicate that beyond all the celebrations, this revision also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

In a recent development, the big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Though it may seem like we just had a massive life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Industry observers note that seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

Industry observers note that starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese Newly introduced Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

It has been revealed that on top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab indicates you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

It has been revealed that this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

In a recent development, of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is presently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

According to recent reports, critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

Industry observers note that monopoly Go has hosted some major names in pop culture for collabs over the years, ranging from K-pop Demon Hunters to The Simpsons. Now, however, they're teaming up with what could be their biggest partnership yet, as Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday arrives on the board starting November 25th!

The Avengers: Doomsday x Monopoly Go collab runs from November 25th all the way to January 27th, and sees you opposing the machinations of Doctor Doom. You'll traverse the masked tyrant's homeland of Latveria in the Doomstadt map, as well as take on the Doomsy in an all-upcoming hero battle.

All in all, a great event for fans of Monopoly Go and the Avengers. I can't be the only one who feels like the marketing blitz for Avengers: Doomsday is trying a bit too hard, though. I remember back when Infinity War and Endgame released, and you didn't need a KFC collab or Monopoly Go even to make it clear what a momentous cinematic moment it was.

Still, even if the movie turns out to be a certified stinker, this event and its runtime from November 25th to January 27th will offer you plenty of time to grab all the rewards and experience all the content that this upcoming crossover event has to offer!

In the meantime, if you'd prefer to keep your puzzling instincts sharp with some other fare, then (say it with me, folks) we've got you covered! Just take a look at our list of the best puzzle games for Android to see some more choice picks we've collected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting.
  • Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek.
  • All members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a latest employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV.

Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words.

All members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ. "Our structure is quite flat, and we elect leaders when needed," Willis told Vertical Slice in a separate interview. "Financially, this means we are not subject to investor demands and the preservation of the company and the jobs it sustains is paramount over needless growth and our 'capital' doesn't compete for returns with other potential investments.".

All of which is obviously gesturing towards the horse elephant in the room: Microsoft, who've made enormous cuts to their Xbox biz in their eagerness to further supercharge their $4 trillion market value.

It has been revealed that "We've replicated some things, changed some things, and added others [from our id Software days]," Willis went on. "Overall, I think top-down hierarchy is something we all have bad experiences with—we also don't want to trend chase or make a game by focus group. We want to make the kinds of classic gameplay focused games that we would play ourselves. We think there is a market for that and our experiences with the gaming community in our past work history informs that.".

According to recent reports, willis's hope is that the "flat" structure will motivate staff to work harder, because they feel like they have a meaningful say over the company's direction. "It allows all ideas to be considered and means we don't miss out on any contributions from our employees just because they don't sit high up in some arbitrary hierarchy," he said..

I'm cynical about "flat" tech giant structures, myself. I think they are very often just an excuse for the biggest egos in a company to throw their weight around. It can work given a friendly initial mix of founders, but it gets complicated when you start hiring upcoming people who don't have the same chemistry. Mind you, there are no plans to expand the company dramatically for the foreseeable. "We want to create a vehicle that allows us to make games for our livelihoods, not to make crazy profits and get 100x returns," Willis went on. I'm also a bit leery of the fact that Hidden Horses have popped up a Kickstarter, because I'm leery about crowd-funding in general, even when Peter Molyneux isn't involved. The studio founders are right now working on some promotional initiatives to drum up support, including a studio documentary and *squints* a promotional beer? Still, I'm happy to hear that at least a few Cacodemon wranglers jettisoned by the major M have landed on their hooves feet. I wish Hidden Horses the best of luck with it all. As for Danger Pay, proper screens, footage and release details are to follow.

In a recent development, halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free revision this winter, an Xbox Wire post announces. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.

Firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

Enhancement [Fri 20th Nov 2026, 10:02pm]: GTA 6 publisher Take-Two is now reporting that day one sales reached $3.79 billion USD, while also selling 32.5 million units pre-release. The $3.79 billion figure is based on "manufacturer estimates".

Here's a bit of their statement:.

Recent findings suggest that "Rockstar Games, a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO), is proud to announce that Grand Theft Auto VI day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, setting a newly introduced record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

Original Story: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly smashed all sorts of records within 24 hours of launch, and it's off to a great start on Xbox Series consoles.

As shared by GTA 6 Countdown, GTA 6 has debuted to a near-perfect 99 score on Metacritic (151 reviews), apparently sold 24.5m copies in under 24 hours, and seen 2 million Xbox players take a trip to Latest Zealand to play the game early.

Sensor Tower's sales tracker also estimates $2.36bn (£1.8bn) in revenue from GTA 6 sales, with the console split mostly in favour of PS5, at a 75% to 25% share over Xbox. Still, the data suggests Xbox still took a whopping $588m from 6.15m units sold.

GTA 6 dominated Twitch viewership too, with 50m hours watched and 3.3m viewers during its busiest hour, beating the livestreaming site's previous record (held by Hogwarts Legacy at 1.2m) by more than double.

According to recent reports, beyond all the major numbers we're chucking your way, we've also spotted a lot of praise for the Xbox Series S version of the game. Whilst Digital Foundry was hit-and-miss on the report, the general response online is majorly positive.

It's good news, then, to finally put to bed the lingering question of whether GTA 6 would run well enough on Xbox Series S consoles. Judging by IGN's comparison, it's not all that different of an experience to Sony's flagship PS5 Pro.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

In a recent development, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial new world headlining Version 4.0.

Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

In a recent development, the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Industry observers note that much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two newly introduced 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

In a recent development, her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other fresh arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

Sources indicate that she also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Sources indicate that version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

It has been revealed that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the fresh outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

Sources indicate that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel and video games are a huge focus for Lego right now, so it was really only a matter of time before all three of those worlds combined to create some Marvel Rivals Lego sets. It was also inevitable that once those worlds collided, Jeff would be the first one called up for Lego duty.

No official announcement from Lego just yet, but as is often the case when it comes to upcoming sets tied to popular IP, an image of Jeff’s set has made it out into the world before an official reveal.

According to recent reports, shared by various accounts that leak Lego and collectibles news, the set will simply be a Lego version of Jeff modeled after his default skin in Marvel Rivals, so just the little Land Shark wearing a pink collar with his name engraved on the gold tag. Lego Jeff has a significant smile on his face with his tongue sticking out, and in a world where Lego doesn’t always nail builds where you recreate beloved characters in Lego form, it seems to have nailed the assignment.

It’s reasonably priced too at just $54.99. There’s a Pokemon set out there that costs $650, and Lego’s latest Death Star carries a $1,000 price tag, so Rivals fans can count themselves lucky that this first set isn’t going to leave them wondering whether they need to trade in whatever they use to play Rivals just to be able to afford it.

Sources indicate that you don’t have long to wait for the set’s release either, which likely means an official reveal is coming soon. The Jeff Lego set will be released on January 1, 2027, which tends to be the busiest day of the year for Lego. We already know about the seven new Star Wars sets releasing that day, and there will almost certainly be more announcements made between now and then.

The one thing that hasn’t been revealed via the Jeff set leak is how many pieces it will take to rebuild the Land Shark. We can make an educated guess based on the price of other Marvel sets, though. Taking similarly priced sets into account, it seems likely Lego Jeff will fall somewhere between 400 and 600 pieces.

There’s no guarantee that this is the only Marvel Rivals set we’ll be getting on January 1. It might simply be the only one to have leaked. As is the case with Rivals’ Funko Pops, Lego has an almost endless list of options from which to pull if it wants to make a series of Rivals Lego sets. Not just because of the game's growing roster, but because each of its heroes and villains also has several skins. Lego could focus on Jeff alone, releasing upcoming sets where he’s sporting different looks, releasing one every few months, and be set for years.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While driving down the US-70 post Chapter 2, you may hear a woman crying for help, clad in a bathrobe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto has never shied away from, well, anything really. Political corruption, gang violence, culture clashes, both the underworld and sleazy heights are well within Rockstar’s sights, both in their main campaigns and plethora of side content.

With Grand Theft Auto 6’s small-scale start, it can be easy to forget that, with various side missions here to remind us. One such mission without a name, one I’ll just be calling the Near Fatal Sex Scandal, sees a woman begging for help on the side of the road. Want to learn more, and even how to start it yourself? Let’s get straight to it then.

While driving down the US-70 post Chapter 2, you may hear a woman crying for help, clad in a bathrobe. If you stop to help her, she’ll explain that someone up by the house needs your help, and beg you to follow.

Follow her, and she’ll escort you through a very fancy southern style manor, before approaching a bedroom. She asks for your complete confidentiality before opening the door, revealing her husband, a right-wing politician, unresponsive in a sex swing.

Industry observers note that interact with the body to help her get him down, where she’ll realize he’s already dead. Quick on her feet, she demands you help dispose of the body, pointing you to the river just down the hill as the perfect spot. Pick up the corpse as she rushes you out to continue.

Recent findings suggest that as you carry the body down the hill, the politician himself will begin to stir, startling the player character, who drops him to the grass. Stunned and betrayed by his wife’s seeming attempt on his life, he’ll demand you back him up. Follow him back to the estate and allow him to interact with the bedroom door.

His wife, again not missing a beat, immediately pivots back into their roleplay, belittling him and yanking her “bad little globalist” back into the bedroom. For your trouble (and trauma), you’re tossed a cool $10,000, an absolute game changer if found early enough in Chapter 2.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is back to its seams with all kinds of small encounters like this, perfect for a quick joke and a pocket full of cash as you pursue Jason and Lucia’s perfect life.

"One of those ways where you can use AI ethically": CDPR have modified Geralt's Polish voice in The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past with genAI, due to actor's stroke

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion.
  • Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted".
  • It has been revealed that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. The move's been made with the permission of Geralt's Polish voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, and is rooted in the studio wanting his new lines to sound similar to the ones he recorded for the original game prior to having a stroke which has altered how he sounds.

Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted". With next year's Songs of the Past expansion, CD Projekt Red were seemingly more concerned about making sure lines recorded by post-stroke Rozenek don't sound markedly different to those he recorded a decade ago for the base game and its existing expansions.

It has been revealed that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings. Rozenek reportedly gave his blessing for this to go ahead. "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," he told Game File. "I have great trust...for the creators of this game.".

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red have enlisted Respeecher's services. Back in 2023, it was revealed that the studio had used speech synthesis software to make ripperdoc Viktor Vektor's lines in the Polish version of Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion sound like actor Miłogost Reczek. Reczek died in 2021 before he could reprise his role as Vektor for the DLC, so rather than recasting the character across the whole game to avoid noticeable differences in voice, CD Projekt got another actor to voice Vektor's latest lines for Phantom Liberty, then used the genAI tech to make those lines sound like Reczek was delivering them. CD Projekt Red mentioned at the time that they'd gotten permission from Reczek's family before going ahead with their initiative.

Speaking to Game File about this latest use of genAI on Rozenek's Songs of the Past lines, CD Projekt localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed noted that "as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a major concern". "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," he added. The argument the studio are making at current is that this was "a special case" due to Rozenek's specific situation with Songs of the Past.

Geralt's English voice actor Doug Cockle reportedly won't have his lines for the new expansion get the same genAI treatment, nor will any lines Rozenek records for future Witcher games, with the studio seemingly happy to lean on the passage of in-game time as an explanation for Geralt sounding different in the latter case.

Industry observers note that as ever, there's a debate to be had as to whether CD Projekt Red should have simply recast Rozenek's role in Songs of the Past if the difference bothered them so, possibly while bringing the actor on to help tutor whomever his human replacement for Songs of the Past would be in nailing the exact gravelly tone needed for Geralt. That way, you'd have two actors being paid for work rather than forking out for genAI instead of one of them, though it's possibly an idea that'd only work well in theory. If I were Rozenek I'm not sure I'd be totally happy aiding someone who could potentially be tapped to replace me going forwards, though it does very much seem like the lesser of two evils when compared to the potential of voice actors being replaced by genAI line readings.

As far as the game alone is concerned, I'm also not sure Geralt's voice being different in the new expansion is something that'd bother me too much when playing. One would assume he'd not suddenly be sounding like a member of Alvin and the Chipmunks, and there are plenty of storyline justifications you could concoct or lean on for him sounding that bit gruffer at times.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

Industry observers note that the Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

According to recent reports, the first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

It has been revealed that badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

In a recent development, heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

According to recent reports, nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

Industry observers note that that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was one of a handful of games brave enough to launch on 'GTA Day' last week, but while Rockstar has been swimming in positive reception ever since, Isaac's re-release hasn't been so lucky.

Indeed, the game has been subject to a hefty review bombing from players on Steam after it was discovered that AI-generated music was used in the release's newly introduced GTA 6-themed online mode (thanks for the heads up, Steam Hype).

A post on the game's Reddit page by user ShweetsStuff alerted players to mentions of the AI music 'tool' Suno in select tracks' metadata, pointing out that no AI disclosure was given on its Steam page (a requirement these days).

As you might expect, players weren't all that happy to learn of the AI usage. At the time of writing, the game's ~1,800 recent reviews lean heavily into the platform's 'Overwhelmingly Negative' camp.

Even the game's original creator, Edmund McMillen, was shocked to learn of the Suno involvement in the game, taking to X to share the following message:.

Woke up to a s**t show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

All fingers point towards publisher Nicalis on this one, then (a company with hardly the best track record when it comes to the treatment of its staff). The studio has since issued a patch on Steam — without any kind of apology, we should add — which removes the GenAI tracks, though it will naturally take longer to make its way to consoles.

Have you already checked out Repentance+ on Switch? Does this put you off doing so? Let us know in the comments.

[source reddit.com, via steamhype.com].

10 Fighting Game Remakes That Improved Everything From The Original Games

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1461 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I still look back fondly on those afternoons at my grandmother's house, sitting in front of the TV with my cousins and firing up my PlayStation 1 for hours of fighting games like Tekken 3—a series I'm still playing with Tekken 8—and Mortal Kombat Trilogy, one of the best games with non-stop violence that ever existed.
  • Recent findings suggest that still, the genre hasn't always been perfect.
  • According to recent reports, fortunately, some of those games got a second chance through exceptional remakes that fixed every flaw from the originals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I still look back fondly on those afternoons at my grandmother's house, sitting in front of the TV with my cousins and firing up my PlayStation 1 for hours of fighting games like Tekken 3—a series I'm still playing with Tekken 8—and Mortal Kombat Trilogy, one of the best games with non-stop violence that ever existed.

Recent findings suggest that still, the genre hasn't always been perfect. Plenty of classics launched with serious balance challenges, rough performance, or questionable mechanics that could easily sour the experience.

According to recent reports, fortunately, some of those games got a second chance through exceptional remakes that fixed every flaw from the originals. Here are 10 fighting games that completely reinvented themselves with fresh mechanics, features and definitive balancing.

It has been revealed that as a longtime JoJo's Bizarre Adventure fan, I was excited when All-Star Battle got its Western PS3 release in 2014 (following its 2013 Japanese debut). That hype faded fast once I felt its 30 fps frame rate, slower combat pacing, and a Campaign mode weighed down by stamina timers and microtransactions.

In a recent development, in 2022, Bandai Namco released JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: All-Star Battle R on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, and PC. While the Switch version runs at 30 fps, the PlayStation, Xbox, and PC editions target 60 fps, immediately making combat feel snappier to me. It also added an Assist system for extending combos and expanded the roster across the series.

Best of all, it dropped the original Campaign's stamina timers and energy purchases—though the game still features paid DLC characters and costumes, and solo players lost the original Story and Campaign modes in favor of the panel-based All-Star Battle mode. For me, the faster gameplay made that trade-off worth it.

Not every necessary remake is modern. While the 1993 arcade Virtua Fighter was a landmark title, its 1994 Sega Saturn port was rough, with flat, untextured polygonal models and distracting polygon flickering.

Released in 1995 for arcades and the Saturn, Virtua Fighter Remix tackled those early-port issues head-on. Side by side on Saturn, the jump is clear: Remix introduced texture-mapped character models with far sharper facial and outfit detail. It wasn't a flawless fix—some polygon glitches remained, the lighting shifted, and load times increased—but for Saturn owners at the time, it was still a major visual upgrade that stood up much better alongside early Tekken.

Sources indicate that after falling in love with Bloody Roar 2, playing Bloody Roar 3 on PS2 (following its 2000 arcade debut) left me wanting more. Its animal-transformation premise was still a blast, but to my eyes, the early-PS2 visuals looked rough, with jagged edges and coarse textures.

In 2002, Bloody Roar: Primal Fury introduced on Nintendo GameCube (followed by Bloody Roar Extreme on Xbox in 2003) as an enhanced remake of Bloody Roar 3. Compared to the PS2 release, the GameCube version offered cleaner character models, upgraded lighting, animated endings for the cast, and newcomers like Cronos and Ganesha. Personally, it became my go-to way to play the game, making every match feel far more polished and satisfying.

I've loved Street Fighter for years, but jumping into specific Western arcade revisions of 1994's Super Street Fighter II Turbo—notably the World 940223 and USA 940323 builds—was a rude awakening. Both are notorious for a difficulty bug that makes the CPU unusually fierce regardless of the machine's setting, on top of lopsided matchups involving Old Sagat, Vega, and a tournament-banned Akuma.

Sources indicate that when Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix hit PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2008, I was immediately won over. Udon Entertainment redrew the sprites and stages in HD, and the game added a rebalanced mode to rein in dominant fighters while still letting purists play under the original rules. Paired with built-in GGPO rollback netcode, it became a much friendlier way to enjoy a classic.

The PS2 introduced me to countless classics, including Dead or Alive 2: Hardcore (an updated PS2 edition of the 1999 arcade and 2000 Dreamcast fighter). I loved its fast pace and multi-tiered stages, though its early-PS2 visuals aged quickly and its counter-heavy combat could feel unforgiving.

Industry observers note that dead or Alive Ultimate arrived on the original Xbox in 2004 with a ground-up remake of DOA2 built on an upgraded DOA3 engine. Compared to the PS2 version, the leap in lighting, textures, and stage detail was night and day. While reversals remained a defining—and sometimes divisive—part of the formula, Ultimate felt like the definitive package, bringing together fighters like Tengu and Bayman alongside DOA3's Hitomi and over 20 interactive stages.

At launch, it also stood out for its Xbox Live lobbies and spectator mode—a huge draw at the time, even though Microsoft officially shut down original Xbox Live servers in April 2010.

According to recent reports, SNK's catalog deserves a spot in any fighting game discussion, including The King of Fighters 2002. This fantastic Neo Geo game had strong core gameplay, but its presentation felt more stripped-back to me than SNK's earlier classics, with a soundtrack that didn't hit as hard and several NESTS-saga favorites missing from the roster.

I also wasn't a fan of a meta dominated by Billy Kane, Athena, and Choi. That's why the 2009 remake, The King of Fighters 2002: Unlimited Match (originally on PS2, later coming to Xbox Live Arcade in 2010 and PC in 2015), felt like such a triumph.

Expanding the roster to 66 playable characters in its console and Xbox Live Arcade editions, it overhauled the stages (using 3D polygonal backgrounds on PS2 and 2D replacements on PC), added a newly introduced soundtrack, refined MAX Mode cancels, and introduced new moves across the cast—turning it into one of my favorite 2D fighters SNK has ever made.

The original Karateka introduced in 1984 for the Apple II before receiving ports for Atari 8-bit systems, the NES/Famicom, and the Commodore 64. Its flaws stood out promptly, though: the controls were slow and stiff, there were no checkpoints—meaning a single lost fight sent you right back to the beginning—and the combat system was bare-bones.

In 2012, however, a remake arrived on Xbox 360 before making its way to PC, PS3, and iOS. This new version rebuilt the visuals from the ground up in cel-shaded 3D powered by Unreal Engine 3, and introduced a one-on-one combat system built around visual and audio cues for countering attacks. What really won me over was how it replaced the single-life structure with three consecutive suitors, each with different speeds and their own unique endings.

Sources indicate that at launch, the original Fatal Fury: King of Fighters—released in 1991 for Neo Geo—drew plenty of criticism for offering only three playable characters: Andy Bogard, Terry Bogard, and Joe Higashi. On top of that, its gameplay lacked depth, relying on a simple three-button control scheme.

In 1999, Fatal Fury: Wild Ambition hit the Hyper Neo Geo 64 and PlayStation 1, expanding the roster to 12 fighters in arcades and 14 on PS1. It also introduced fresh defensive and meter-management mechanics, including the Heat Meter, Heat Blow, and Overdrive Power. It's worth noting, however, that Sony's console version took several noticeable graphical downgrades compared to the arcade release.

In a recent development, this title might not be as widely known as others on this list, but it had a strong following in Japan back in the day. Asuka 120% Burning Fest. originally rolled out in 1994 for the FM Towns, though several concerns held the experience back—including a limited roster, a lack of defensive tools, and the fact that it was locked to a niche Japanese home computer.

Several years later, in 1999, Asuka 120% Final: Burning Fest. Final arrived on PS1. While it remained a Japan-only release, this version featured a completely rebuilt combat engine with a much faster pace and noticeably smoother sprite animations. It also expanded the character roster—adding secret fighters into the mix—and introduced deeper offensive and defensive mechanics, such as air recovery.

It has been revealed that the original Eternal Champions introduced on the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive in 1993 in North America, followed by Europe and Japan in 1994. Like many entries on this list, though, it suffered from frustrating challenges—including punishing AI, clunky, unintuitive controls, and a small roster, among other flaws.

It wasn't until 1995 that its remake, Eternal Champions: Challenge from the Dark Side, which can be considered one of the best fighting games stuck on older systems, arrived on the Sega CD as an expanded overhaul of the original. It expanded the starting roster from nine to 13 fighters—alongside a large lineup of unlockables—introduced latest FMV finishers called Cinekills, and improved the difficulty curve compared to the original game.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing problems with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.
  • We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the fresh content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing problems with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

Sources indicate that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the fresh season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

Industry observers note that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Sources indicate that movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

In a recent development, the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

In a recent development, what we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Prepares lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

In a recent development, echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

In a recent development, we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first upcoming class in 25 years.

In a recent development, reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as latest quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Breaking: Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while.
  • According to recent reports, instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news.
  • Recent findings suggest that also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while. But I come back to you now at the turn of the technological tide. Well, sort of. Sadly I'm not here to predict an end to the ridiculous AI-fuelled chip crisis. That whole mess has a couple of years to run, surely.

According to recent reports, instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news. In short, have you seen how cheap PC gaming monitors are? I mean remarkably, almost stupendously, cheap. I'm talking £60 / $60 for an entry-level 1080p panel with triple-digit refresh rate, sub-£200 / $250 for high-refresh 4K gaming. Heck, even OLED monitors now start with a "2" in both currencies.

Recent findings suggest that also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years. A 4K panel bought today for £200 is equivalent to paying roughly £150 back in 2020. All the while, that same £200 / $200 right now won't buy you a current-model gaming graphics card at all, even the most feeble example, and will barely secure a basic dual-channel 16GB DDR5 memory kit. Youch.

According to recent reports, so, I think we can all agree monitors are cheap in the current chip-catastrophe context. The immediate question is why? The answer isn't all that complicated, actually. Most obviously, the display market isn't being devoured by the AI craze. All those data centres are stuffed with GPUs, memory chips and NAND flash, not monitors.

By way of example, one of the largest new AI data centres on Earth is Microsoft's new Fairwater site in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin. It's thought to pack hundreds of thousands of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs. The cost doesn't bear thinking about, but those GPUs are built into what's known as "headless" server racks. In other words, they have no screens at all. Ultimately, the key compute hardware is all managed remotely, in which capacity the Fairwater facility is reported to currently have around 375 employees. If we generously assume each has two PC monitors, that's only 750 for the entire site.

Industry observers note that AI isn't really driving demand on the end-user side of the equation, either. Put it this way: you don't need to buy a upcoming phone, laptop or PC to access the latest models. At the same time, the display market is suffering from something of a glut of overcapacity. Chinese companies built out huge capacity in LCD panel manufacturing over the past decade, to the extent factories are now running underutilised. Meanwhile, even the OLED market is arguably oversupplied.

In a recent development, in fact, Samsung and LG, the two major noises in large OLED panel manufacturing (as opposed to OLED displays for tablets and phones), have been shifting emphasis away from TV panels to PC monitors because the latter offer better margins. Meanwhile, the AI boom has almost definitely meant lower demand for fresh PCs. Certainly, the big research houses point to cratering PC sales thanks to higher component costs. Long story short, that's oodles of capacity combined with weakening demand. Like I stated, the explanation for cheap monitors isn't exactly rocket surgery, if you know what I mean.

What is a bit more complicated is making sense of what's available today in the gaming monitor market. With so much choice, where exactly is the very best value to be found? And are there any remaining pain points?

Monitor specifications, to be sure, can be tricksy at the best of times. But if you're looking for some blanket rules to fling casually over the whole LCD monitor market - I'll be digging deeper into OLED tech another day - try these for size. Look for, at minimum, 300 nits brightness and 1ms response times. Refresh rates are a slightly more complicated call, but for the vast majority of games, 144Hz is plenty. For "esports-grade multiplayer fare like Counter-Strike or Dota 2, or I think a refresh in the high 200s will get the job done for most. If you'll benefit from more than that, you almost certainly know who you are already.

According to recent reports, oh, and heavily favour IPS over VA panels. Exceptions exist: there are some decent "Rapid VA" panels these days and Samsung, in particular, does some nippy VA models. But a lot of the cheaper stuff is pretty slow and smeary, making VA a risky buy. Finally, don't worry too much about claimed HDR capability, save for the fact that HDR 400 certification at least means the monitor can do 400 nits. Unless a monitor has local dimming, it won't be truly HDR capable.

Anywho, one immediate and rather ironic problem is the growing mismatch between monitors and GPUs. For sure, it's great you can grab a high-refresh 4K monitor for such little money. It's almost hard to believe that you can have this 27-inch IPS MSI for sub-£200 (you're looking at $250 for the same model in the US), and it even has a 288Hz 1080p dual mode.

I actually favour 32 inches with my 4K gaming, and that's naturally a little pricier, especially if you insist on an IPS - which again, you probably should. But even $350 for that kind of panel (here's a comparable model for £340 in the UK) is a fraction of what you'd have paid for a similarly specced model a few years ago. And it probably wouldn't have included dual-mode functionality.

Here's the problem, though. How are you going to drive the thing, what with its eight million-plus pixels? After all, the cheapest RTX 5090 on Newegg right now is over $6,500. So high-end Nvidia GPUs now cost about as much as a decent used car.

It has been revealed that of course, you might be surprised just how effective the likes of an AMD RX 9070 XT or Nvidia RTX 5070-class GPU is at 4K thanks to upscaling technologies including DLSS and FSR. The latest transformer model upscalers really do knock out pretty stellar image quality. Add in a bit of frame gen and you have a compelling combination of visual sharpness, reasonably low latency and nice smoothframe rates, even in the most demanding of games. Perhaps the one thing you can't do is enable full path tracing in a game like Cyberpunk 2077 and still expect a slick experience, but standard ray tracing remains an option.

The bigger snag, unsurprisingly, is that you can no longer bag a 5070 at (let alone below) its original £539 / $549 MSRP. Instead, you're looking at the thick end of £800 / $900. That's a bit of an ask for pairing with a £200 monitor, isn't it?

I'd therefore argue that, for pure gaming purposes, the bang-for-buck sweet spot remains just where it's been sat twiddling its thumbs for the better part of a decade, namely 1440p. That applies to both its vanilla 16:9 aspect variety and my personally preferred ultrawide format, the latter being so very immersive and also pretty nifty for daily multi-tasking. Indeed, the 27-inch 1440p segment even brings the vibrant colours and infinite contrast of OLED panels into a reasonably affordable window.

Sources indicate that by way of example, £179 (or $150) is enough for a circa 200Hz, IPS 1440p panel with super low (by IPS standards) pixel response, even if the 250-nit brightness is lower than I'd like. Meanwhile, as I write these words, pricing for big-brand 27-inch 1440p gaming OLEDs kicks off at about £290 in the UK and roughly $270 in the US. Admittedly, those entry-level OLEDs come with some compromises, which I'll cover in a forthcoming post. But what you might call 'proper' OLED panels can be had around the low £300 / $300 mark - not throw-away money, for sure, but relatively accessible.

Recent findings suggest that the 34-inch 1440p ultrawide segment is a bit trickier, however. The good news is that conventional LCD models can be had for relative peanuts, with prices starting at about £220 or $249 for game-focused, high-refresh models. But those two example both use a VA panel, which usually means inferior pixel response.

IPS models are a little thin on the ground when it comes to 34-inch ultrawide, but sneaking in below £300 / $300 is generally possible. The real bummer is OLED, where going ultrawide invokes a massive premium. The best price I can find on a big-brand 34-inch ultrawide today is $629 for this Asus model in the US and £648 for this MSI option in the UK.

That's awfully toppy, especially when you consider that you can grab a 49-inch, 5,120x1,440 ultrawide OLED for barely any more money. I do actually quite like those 49-inch ultrawides, but I have to concede the ergonomics are challenging. However, 4K OLEDs in 27-inch and 32-inch formats can also be had for as much as £100 / $100 less than the current cheapest 34-inch 1440p ultrawides, which doesn't make much sense to me.

Again, with 4K, there's the challenge of keeping all those pixels updated. If you already have a sufficiently mighty graphics card, though, I a 32-inch 4K OLED can make a fantastic all-round option, and something like this MSI model for £549 would be absolutely lovely. You get good pixel density and lots of space for daily desktopping, plus OLED visuals and a large enough panel to be really get you into your games.

It's just a pity that 34-inch OLED ultrawides remain so weirdly expensive, it being a format that ticks so many different boxes. As for my own personal money-no-object pick, well, I'm typing these words on the latest Alienware AW3926QW, the 39-inch 5K2K beast with a Tandem WOLED panel and RGB subpixels.

According to recent reports, one could argue it's a relative steal at £1,079 or $1,100. I mean, it's pretty much peak current PC gaming display technology, and it's about half the price of what Nvidia's second-tier RTX 5080 graphics card is going for lately. Assuming you can even find one in stock.

It has been revealed that at this point, the one major category I haven't covered is LCD monitors with mini-LED full-array local dimming. Cards on the table, I'm not a huge fan of mini-LED monitors. The detailed reasons for that are, perhaps, the subject for another day. But I've reviewed countless models and have yet to see one that didn't come with pretty serious compromises.

That mentioned, the technology has gotten a lot more accessible in the last 12 to 18 months, to the extent that 27-inch 1440p models start at just over $250. I've had that specific model in and came away pretty impressed. It's very, very punchy, and even factoring in the limitations of mini-LED versus OLED when it comes to lighting control and speed, I cannot deny the temptation.

According to recent reports, just for completeness, one further exception to the general rule of cheap gaming monitors involves ultra-high refresh monitors aimed at serious esports aficionados. I'm talking about panels like this 1,000Hz LG I sampled elsewhere. At £800 / $1,000 for a 25-inch 1080p IPS panel it's inevitably a niche proposition, and poor value by normal standards.

I think a much better compromise for just about everyone, short of an actual esports pro, is to grab a larger, higher resolution monitor that offers one of those windowed 1080p modes running at about 500Hz or thereabouts. That way you've got a nice high-res panel for both work and play, as well as that ultra-low latency mode for when you want to dance around Dust 2 doling out the headshots or whatever.

According to recent reports, incidentally, I realise I've gone in a bit hot and heavy with the OLED content here, the implicit assumption being OLED is all that, and notably without addressing the obvious objections like the risk of burn-in. But all that, I hope you'll be pleased to hear, is very much the subject for my next RPS post on all things OLED.

Industry observers note that until then, all I can say is thank goodness PC monitors provide relative respite from the parlous state of much of the rest of the PC component market. It's absolutely brutal out there if you're building a gaming PC, but at least you'll get a lot of screen for your money.

Just to round things out, if anyone has any specific queries at any given price point, form factor or panel type, shout out below and I'll try to steer you in the direction of a decent model.
